files.Dockerfile:
# The voice-E2E engine, fully containerized — this is exactly what a Fly
# tester machine would run. Bundled Chromium (headless), API TTS for the
# mouth, element-tap ears, Stagehand brain. No local Chrome, no macOS.
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends espeak-ng ffmpeg \
  && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /e2e
COPY package.json ./
RUN npm install
# npm may resolve a newer Playwright than the image's preinstalled browsers —
# install the matching Chromium build for whatever version we got.
RUN npx playwright install chromium
COPY playwright.config.ts ./
COPY lib ./lib
COPY specs ./specs
COPY fixtures ./fixtures
COPY scripts ./scripts
COPY scenarios ./scenarios

ARG HARNESS_SHA=dev
ENV HARNESS_SHA=$HARNESS_SHA
EXPOSE 8080
ENV OSBORN_TEST_CONTAINER=1
ENV LIVE_STREAM_PORT=8080
# Keys at runtime: -e OPENAI_API_KEY -e GOOGLE_API_KEY -e DEEPGRAM_API_KEY
# (on Fly these come from `fly secrets`). OSBORN_TEST_SPEC picks the spec.
CMD ["sh", "scripts/fly-run.sh"]
files.fly.toml:
# Voice-E2E tester machine. Run-on-start: `fly machine start` (or the Machines
# API) boots it, it runs OSBORN_TEST_SPEC, stores artifacts on the volume at
# /data/runs/<timestamp>/, then exits and the machine stops — billing only
# while a test is actually running.
app = "osborn-voice-e2e"
primary_region = "ord"

[env]
  # Site-knowledge profiles (cached actions) persist on the volume — the
  # tester machine gets smarter/cheaper with every run.
  OSBORN_KNOWLEDGE_DIR = "/data/knowledge"

[build]
  dockerfile = "Dockerfile"

[[mounts]]
  source = "e2e_results"
  destination = "/data"

[[restart]]
  policy = "never"

[[vm]]
  size = "shared-cpu-2x"
  memory = "2048mb"

# Live browser stream (CDP screencast → MJPEG) served during a run.
[http_service]
  internal_port = 8080
  force_https = true
  auto_stop_machines = false
  auto_start_machines = false
  min_machines_running = 0
files..gitignore:
node_modules/
test-results/
playwright-report/
results/
profiles/
knowledge/
*.wav
*.webm
*.m4a

files.lib/perception.ts:
import type { Page } from '@playwright/test'
import { waitForSpeechEvent } from './steps'
import { hearSince, screenTail } from './converse'

/**
 * PERCEPTION BUNDLE — the generic sensory pipeline the user described:
 *
 *   sound detected (speech-start event, default RMS threshold)
 *     → we're already recording (always-on)
 *     → sound stops (speech-stop)
 *     → package the CLIP as one bundle: audio transcript of exactly that
 *       window + screenshot + visible text
 *     → hand the whole bundle to the brain in one shot
 *
 * Nothing here references Osborn/voice-native selectors or behaviors — it's
 * media-element energy + pixels + text, so it works on any app that makes
 * sound (or with video: any app at all). One system, not two: the brain's
 * decision input is audio + visuals together.
 */

export type Perception = {
  heard: string // words spoken during the event window (audio, not captions)
  screenshotB64: string // what the screen looked like as the sound ended
  screenText: string // visible text tail (cheap context)
  startedAt: number // capture-relative ms
  endedAt: number
}

/**
 * Wait for the next audio event and return its full perception bundle.
 * `tCaptureStart` = epoch ms when startElementCapture began (for
 * capture-relative word timestamps).
 */
export async function perceiveNextUtterance(
  page: Page,
  tCaptureStart: number,
  opts?: { startTimeoutMs?: number; stopTimeoutMs?: number; settleMs?: number },
): Promise<Perception> {
  const sinceMs = Date.now() - tCaptureStart
  const startT = await waitForSpeechEvent(page, 'speech-start', opts?.startTimeoutMs ?? 90_000)
  const stopT = await waitForSpeechEvent(page, 'speech-stop', opts?.stopTimeoutMs ?? 120_000).catch(() => Date.now())
  await page.waitForTimeout(opts?.settleMs ?? 800) // let captions/UI catch up
  const [heard, shot, text] = await Promise.all([
    hearSince(page, sinceMs).catch(() => ''),
    page.screenshot({ type: 'jpeg', quality: 60 }).then((b) => b.toString('base64')),
    screenTail(page),
  ])
  return {
    heard,
    screenshotB64: shot,
    screenText: text,
    startedAt: startT - tCaptureStart,
    endedAt: stopT - tCaptureStart,
  }
}
files.scenarios/auth-signout.yaml:
name: auth-signout
description: >
  DELIBERATE-ONLY (destroys the saved profile session): from the logged-in
  dashboard, sign out, verify the landing page. Requires OSBORN_ALLOW_SIGNOUT=1
  and a saved profile; re-run scripts/save-profile.ts after each use.
room: false
profile: osbornojure
url: "/dashboard"
requiresEnv: OSBORN_ALLOW_SIGNOUT
steps:
  - pause: 4000
  - assertScreen: "new conversation|recent|settings"
  - act: "Open the user profile or account menu and choose sign out / log out"
  - pause: 5000
  - assertScreen: "sign in|log in|continue with|get started"

room: false
profile: osbornojure
url: "/dashboard"
steps:
  - pause: 4000
  - assertScreen: "osborn|new conversation|environment"
  - pause: 6000
  - assertScreen: "cloud|resume|running|starting"
  - act: "Open the settings area if there is a settings control visible"
  - pause: 3000
  - act: "Return to the main dashboard view if a panel or settings screen is open"
  - pause: 2000
  - act: "Click the New conversation button or the most recent conversation in the recent list"
  - pause: 12000
  - assertScreen: "connecting|listening|previous sessions|resuming|starting"
  - pause: 5000
files.scenarios/end-conversation.yaml:
name: end-conversation
description: End a conversation gracefully — goodbye by voice, then exit the room via the UI and verify a clean landing.
entry: fresh
conversation:
  goal: >
    Say hello and confirm the assistant can hear you. After its reply, say a
    clear goodbye (e.g. that you're done for now, thanks) and end. Max 2
    things said by you.
  maxTurns: 2
  minAudibleReplies: 1
after:
  - pause: 3000
  - act: "Find and click the control that LEAVES or ENDS the voice session (a leave button, hang-up icon, or disconnect control). Do not use browser navigation."
  - pause: 6000
  - assertScreen: "new conversation|dashboard|sign in|get started|osborn"

files.scripts/fly-run.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# Fly tester-machine entrypoint: run the requested spec, persist artifacts to
# the volume, exit 0 so the machine stops (restart policy "never" — a failing
# TEST must not put the machine in a restart loop; the result lives in the
# artifacts + exit-code file).
SPEC="${OSBORN_TEST_SPEC:-specs/stagehand-conversation.spec.ts}"
echo "[fly-run] harness version: ${HARNESS_SHA:-unknown}"
echo "[fly-run] running $SPEC"
npx playwright test "$SPEC"
code=$?
echo "[fly-run] exit code: $code"
if [ -d /data ]; then
  ts=$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
  dest="/data/runs/$ts"
  mkdir -p "$dest"
  cp -r test-results "$dest/" 2>/dev/null
  cp -r playwright-report "$dest/" 2>/dev/null
  cp -r results "$dest/" 2>/dev/null
  echo "$code" > "$dest/exit-code"
  echo "[fly-run] artifacts stored in $dest"
  # rolling metrics file across all runs
  mkdir -p /data
  cat results/runs.jsonl >> /data/history.jsonl 2>/dev/null
fi
# Optional: stay alive briefly after the run so artifacts can be pulled via
# fly ssh sftp before the machine stops (OSBORN_HOLD_AFTER=seconds).
if [ -n "$OSBORN_HOLD_AFTER" ]; then
  echo "[fly-run] holding machine open for ${OSBORN_HOLD_AFTER}s for artifact retrieval"
  sleep "$OSBORN_HOLD_AFTER"
fi
exit 0
files.scripts/make-fixtures.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# Generate spoken WAV fixtures for the fake-mic harness.
#
# Chromium's --use-file-for-fake-audio-capture wants WAV (PCM). On macOS we
# synthesize with `say` (AIFF) then convert with afconvert (both built in).
# On Linux CI, espeak-ng + sox produce the same thing.
#
# Each fixture starts with ~1s of silence so the connection settles before
# speech begins (Deepgram VAD needs the utterance, not the join click).
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../fixtures"

gen() {
  name=$1; text=$2; pad=${3:-5}
  if command -v say >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    say -o "_$name.aiff" "$text"
    afconvert -f WAVE -d LEI16@44100 -c 1 "_$name.aiff" "_$name.wav"
    rm -f "_$name.aiff"
  elif command -v espeak-ng >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    espeak-ng -w "_$name.wav" "$text"
  else
    echo "need macOS 'say' or espeak-ng" >&2; exit 1
  fi
  # REAL leading silence — the fake mic starts playing at getUserMedia-open,
  # several seconds before LiveKit publish + Deepgram are actually listening.
  # (Learned the hard way: without this pad, only the last word arrives.)
  python3 - "$name" "$pad" << 'PYEOF'
import wave, sys
name, pad = sys.argv[1], float(sys.argv[2])
src = wave.open(f"_{name}.wav", "rb")
params = src.getparams()
silence = b"\x00" * int(params.framerate * pad) * params.sampwidth * params.nchannels
out = wave.open(f"{name}.wav", "wb")
out.setparams(params)
out.writeframes(silence)
out.writeframes(src.readframes(src.getnframes()))
out.close(); src.close()
PYEOF
  rm -f "_$name.wav"
  echo "built $name.wav (${pad}s lead-in)"
}

gen hello-question   "Osborn, this is an automated voice test, code purple elephant. Please reply with the single word pineapple." 6
gen followup-recall  "What word did I just ask you to say?"
gen barge-in-long    "Tell me a very long story about the history of computers, with as much detail as possible."

echo "fixtures ready: $(ls *.wav | tr '\n' ' ')"
files.scripts/save-profile.ts:
/**
 * One-time profile capture (Playwright storageState pattern — the industry
 * standard for "test credentials without sharing the real account"):
 *
 *   npx tsx scripts/save-profile.ts
 *
 * Opens a headed Chrome at the app's landing page. YOU log in once (Google
 * OAuth, the real account). When the dashboard appears, the script saves the
 * SESSION (cookies + localStorage) to profiles/osbornojure/state.json —
 * NOT the Gmail credentials. Tester agents then start already-authenticated:
 *
 *   const context = await browser.newContext({ storageState: 'profiles/osbornojure/state.json' })
 *
 * They can see the dashboard, click around, resume sessions — everything the
 * user sees — with zero access to the underlying Google account. Refresh by
 * re-running this script when the session expires. profiles/ is gitignored.
 */
import { chromium } from '@playwright/test'
import { mkdirSync } from 'fs'
import { join, dirname } from 'path'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'url'

const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))
const APP_URL = process.env.OSBORN_APP_URL || 'https://www.voice-native.com'
const OUT = join(__dirname, '..', 'profiles', 'osbornojure', 'state.json')

const browser = await chromium.launch({ channel: 'chrome', headless: false })
const context = await browser.newContext()
const page = await context.newPage()
await page.goto(APP_URL)
console.log('➡️  Log in in the opened window (Google OAuth). Waiting for the dashboard…')
await page.waitForURL(/dashboard/, { timeout: 300_000 })
await page.waitForTimeout(3_000) // let tokens settle into storage
mkdirSync(dirname(OUT), { recursive: true })
await context.storageState({ path: OUT })
console.log(`✅ Session saved to ${OUT} — tester agents can now start logged in.`)
await browser.close()
